Where Your 200K Tokens Actually Go — and the 60K Version That Works Better
Example budget for a coding agent at turn 12. Anthropic's rule: find the smallest set of high-signal tokens that maximizes the chance of the outcome you want.
BEFORE — everything dumped into one window (example budget)
= 200K tokens • attention is spread across 128K tokens of mostly stale material
AFTER — compaction + just-in-time retrieval + top-3 tools (same task)
= 60K tokens • 70% smaller, rules stay near the top, nothing important lost
Every token competes for attention. Cut
anything the model does not need for the
URLs, queries) in context and load the
content only when the step needs it —
the way Claude Code uses grep and head.
When the window nears its limit,
and next steps; drop raw tool results;
pull them back after compaction — memory
Give exploration to a subagent with a
clean window; it returns a 1-2K token
WHY BIGGER WINDOWS DID NOT SAVE YOU (CONTEXT ROT)
As token count grows, the model's ability to recall and follow instructions degrades — well
before the hard limit. Anthropic calls the usable capacity an 'attention budget'; Chroma
measured the decline across 18 models. The fix is curation, not capacity.
COMPACT WHEN YOU SEE ANY OF THESE
A single tool result larger than ~2KB
More than ~15 turns on one task
The model re-asks something it already knew
You are about to spawn a subagent anyway
Treat context like a budget you spend, not a bucket you fill.
